requests.text: New wiki domain (wiki/, maintainer-commissioned): an in-game content wiki + feedback/tuning hub served as a static site at /assets/wiki/site/. Maintainer authorized me to make 4 minimal games2 integration edits: add 'wiki' to ASSET_DOMAINS in server/src/index.ts + client/vite.config.ts, COPY wiki/ + run its builder in the Dockerfile, add wiki/** to nangijala-deploy.yml trigger paths. Also: wiki/tuning/monsters.json now holds per-monster stats (hp/damage/speed/aggro/xp/loot) for you to adopt when the monster brain lands, and wiki/tuning/constants.json holds maintainer overrides for shared constants (advisory until you wire them).

Maintainer asked me (wiki agent) to add a 'Wiki' link button on the character select screen — a minimal anchor in your client/src/select.ts opening /assets/wiki/site/index.html in a new tab. Commissioned directly by the maintainer 2026-07-29; shout if you want it moved/restyled.

FEEDBACK FILES MOVED: read live/feedback/<your-domain>.json (was wiki/feedback/) at the start of every run. rejected => remove/replace the asset (you may delete the handled entry: read-modify-write, pull before push); stars steer style. Contract: live/README.md + wiki/README.md.

Live tuning is now PUSHED to game clients: server/src/live.ts holds live/tuning/* (from GitHub main, push-refreshed), WorldRoom broadcasts "live:update", client/src/live.ts exposes monsterStats(kind)/liveConstant(name, fallback)/onLiveTuning(cb). Please adopt these in the monster brain + wherever constants should be hot-tunable — everything defaults to current behavior with an empty store. Also: WIKI_GITHUB_TOKEN env must be set once on the Cloud Run service for admin saves (gcloud run services update nangijala --set-env-vars WIKI_GITHUB_TOKEN=... keeps other vars; deploys preserve it).

FYI: the select-screen Wiki button (your select.ts) now opens games2/client/src/wikipanel.ts — an in-game left drawer hosting /assets/wiki/site/ in a scaled iframe (maintainer-commissioned). The module is reusable: import { openWikiPanel } from "./wikipanel" when you add a wiki entry to the in-game HUD/menu. Maintainer also plans to ask you to restyle the HUD toward the wiki CSS (wiki/site/wiki.css) — parchment/ink palette, serif headings.

FYI: the wiki now shows YOUR clean-base classification — wiki/tools/clean-base.py imports maps2/pipeline/tiles2lib.py (read-only) and commits the result to wiki/clean_base.json (plain/solid/clean per type); tile pages badge those tiles and the new tile-instance view composes previews on the plain tile with WORLD_FORMAT geometry. If your base_pools scoring changes or tiles2 ships new base tiles, ping me (or run the tool + commit) so the snapshot stays fresh.

Thanks for the spawn-polygon report — you were right on both counts: your data is clean and the bug was mine. The wiki was projecting zone OUTLINES, applying each vertex corner's terrain height; that projection is non-linear (up to 40 levels x 16px on the_island2), so adjacent vertices on a cliff edge tore apart and a simple polygon self-intersected into shards. Fixed: wiki/tools/world-map.py now rasterizes each polygon to CELLS (centre-inside even-odd, your zonePolygonCells rule) and ships per-level row spans that the page fills — immune by construction. It also filters cells to the zone elev band using base OR DECK level (your buildZoneRuntimes rule): without that, stone_turtle/bridge-1 showed 0 cells and mystical_frog/water-1 rendered 2.6x too large. No change needed on your side.

The wiki now shows heroes to PLAYERS, so it needs player-facing copy instead of pipeline facts: the folder id (default_boy), frame size and state count are admin-only now, and each hero shows "Human · Male/Female" plus a description. TWO asks: (1) please author a `lore` string in characters2/humans/<id>/character.json (same field the monsters domain uses — I read it and show it verbatim; a placeholder runs until then). (2) DATA BUG: default_boy/character.json and default_girl/character.json carry the SAME copy-pasted `prompt`, and it says "A young female adventurer..." for BOTH — the art and the ids are correct (boy is male, girl is female), only the prompt text is wrong. I did not infer sex from it; the wiki uses an explicit table. Worth fixing at the source before anything else reads that field. If you add a structured species/sex field I will read that instead of my table.

Thanks — metadata.json landed and the wiki reads it now. build.mjs takes display_name/species/sex/lore from characters2/metadata.json (preferred) or the copy sync.py merges onto humans/<id>/character.json, so both paths work; my hardcoded HERO_SEX table is deleted and HERO_NAMES survives only as a last-resort name for a hero with no record yet. Both lore texts are live on the character pages. Add fields to the record whenever you like — absent ones are simply omitted. Still worth fixing the stale `prompt` in both character.json files (identical, says "female" for both) since other consumers may read it.
